confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Qu'est-ce que tu as à manger aujourd'hui ? / What did you eat today?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu as mangé aujourd'hui ? / What did you eat today?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: The source target asks what the person has available/to eat today, not what they ate.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Quelle heure vous avez ? / What time do you have?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Quelle heure avez-vous ? / What time do you have?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: Current word order is nonstandard for a polished learner workbook.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Qu'est-ce que tu voulais que je fasse ? / What would you have me do?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu voulais que je fasse ? / What did you want me to do?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: French is past 'wanted'; the English conditional-style prompt is not a tight standalone equivalent.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Pourquoi as-tu besoin de mon aide? / Why do you want my help?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Pourquoi as-tu besoin de mon aide ? / Why do you need my help?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: avoir besoin de means need, not want.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: D'où connaissais-tu mon nom ? / How did you know my name?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Comment connaissais-tu mon nom ? / How did you know my name?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: D'où asks from where/from what source rather than simply how.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: D'où connaissiez-vous mon nom ? / How did you know my name?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Comment connaissiez-vous mon nom ? / How did you know my name?

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Comment aimeriez-vous votre café ? / How do you want your coffee?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Comment voulez-vous votre café ? / How do you want your coffee?

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Qu'est ce que tu as acheté pour ton petit ami ?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu as acheté pour ton petit ami ?

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.observed: Que faisais-tu là-bas ? / What did you do in there?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Que faisais-tu là-bas ? / What were you doing there?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: French imperfect is progressive/background aspect, unlike the English simple past supplied.

confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.recommended: Qu'est-ce que j'ai besoin de savoir ?
confirmed_or_high_confidence_findings.note: The inversion is not valid with avoir besoin in this construction; 'Que dois-je savoir ?' is another natural option.

normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: Space before the question mark is inconsistent with the workbook's other French typography; normalize to one French spacing convention.
Question-mark spacing is inconsistent; define one house style (prefer French typographic spacing) and normalize.
Several elevated/literary subjunctive forms are grammatically possible but may be inappropriate for the intended general learner register; native editorial review should simplify where useful.
fisse is literary imperfect subjunctive and disproportionately advanced/archaic for the surrounding bank.
ce qu'il s'est passé is widespread usage, but ce qui s'est passé is often preferred in edited standard French; choose a house standard rather than silently mixing.
où elle est can legitimately translate 'where it is' when the referent is feminine, but the standalone English is gender-neutral; consider a less context-dependent pair.
qui c'est is idiomatic spoken French; keep only if the workbook intentionally includes conversational register alongside formal variants.
J'ai combien de temps ? is conversational word order; for standard written learner French prefer Combien de temps ai-je ?.
Que puis-je pour votre service ? is highly formal/dated; replace with a contemporary learner phrase such as En quoi puis-je vous aider ? if register consistency is the goal.
encore adds an 'again/what now?' nuance absent from the English 'this time'; review equivalence.
Qu'avez-vous/Qu'as-tu besoin de... is less polished than De quoi avez-vous besoin ? or Qu'est-ce que vous avez besoin de...; review standard-register phrasing.
Mood choice after croire/penser in affirmative questions varies by nuance/register; native-editorial review should normalize without over-correcting legitimate variants.
